title: Additive group torsors over an affine scheme have a section
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be any commutative $k$-algebra, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathbf G_{a,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ with addition [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $P\to S$ be a faithfully flat surjective morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], equipped with a right $\mathbf G_{a,k}$-action over $S$ for which $(p,a)\mapsto(p,p+a)$ is an isomorphism $P\times_k\mathbf G_{a,k}\simeq P\times_SP$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there is an $S$-section $e:S\to P$ of $P\to S$. No Noetherian, reducedness, finite-type-over-$k$, or perfectness hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $k$.

source.place: Example 2.72, printed p.61, the additive torsor assertion for an arbitrary k-algebra R_0, using the exact faithfully flat additive Cech complex.

proof.text: Write $f:P\to S$. By the definition of fppf coverings, the given flat, surjective, finite-presentation map is an fppf singleton covering; it is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-singleton-affine-refinement] to obtain an affine fpqc cover $q:U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to S$ and an $S$-map $h:U\to P$. The affine flatness criterion and the flat-surjective-spectrum criterion show that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. Thus $h$ is an actual local point of the torsor over a faithfully flat algebra, as required in Milne's argument. This also allows $A=0$: then $S$ is empty and the unique map $S\to P$ already is a section.

source.place: Tags 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), 022E (lemma-fpqc-affine); the affine ring criteria are Morphisms Tag 01U5 and Algebra Tag 00HQ.

proof.text: On $U_2=U\times_SU$ let $h_1,h_2$ be the two pullbacks of $h$. Apply the inverse of the torsor isomorphism from the hypothesis to $(h_1,h_2)$. Its second component is the unique morphism $c:U_2\to\mathbf G_{a,k}$ with $h_2=h_1+c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_2=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AB)$ and the triple product has coordinate ring $B\otimes_AB\otimes_AB$. Morphisms from these affine $k$-schemes to $\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ correspond to elements of their coordinate rings: the ring map is determined by the image of $t$, and conversely polynomial evaluation gives that map. The group law in [def-sc-gm-ga] is addition of these elements. On the triple product the action law gives $h_3=(h_1+c_{12})+c_{23}=h_1+(c_{12}+c_{23})$, while $h_3=h_1+c_{13}$. Uniqueness in the torsor isomorphism gives $c_{23}-c_{13}+c_{12}=0$ as an equality in the triple tensor ring. This is precisely the degree-one cocycle equation.

source.place: Example 2.72, printed p.61: additive torsors and the faithfully flat additive Cech complex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-cech-exact] with the faithfully flat map $A\to B$ and the $A$-module $M=A$. Under the canonical identifications $A\otimes_AB=B$ and $A\otimes_AB\otimes_AB=B\otimes_AB$, exactness at $B\otimes_AB$ says that there is $b\in B$ with $c=1\otimes b-b\otimes1$; the next differential is exactly $c\mapsto c_{23}-c_{13}+c_{12}$. Regard $b$ as a morphism $U\to\mathbf G_{a,k}$ by polynomial evaluation, and define $t=h-b:U\to P$ using the given action and the inverse in [def-sc-gm-ga]. On $U_2$ write $b_1=b\otimes1$, $b_2=1\otimes b$. Then $t_2=h_2-b_2=h_1+c-b_2=h_1-b_1=t_1$. Every equality uses the action law, with the displayed coboundary formula fixing the sign. Thus $t$ is a matching morphism on the fpqc cover $q$.

source.place: Tag 023M (lemma-ff-exact), applied in degree one with M=A; Milne Example 2.72, printed p.61.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the fpqc singleton $q:U\to S$, target scheme $P$, and the matching map $t$. It gives a unique morphism $e:S\to P$ with $e\circ q=t$. Since the action is over $S$, we have $f\circ t=q$. Hence $(f\circ e)\circ q=q=\operatorname{id}_S\circ q$. The uniqueness clause of the same descent statement, now with target $S$, implies $f\circ e=\operatorname{id}_S$. Therefore $e$ is the required $S$-section. All inputs above apply to arbitrary commutative $A$ and use no finiteness, reducedness, Noetherian or perfectness assumption beyond the hypotheses stated for $f$.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), existence and uniqueness of morphisms from matching maps.
